audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Naaman, captive girl, Elisha, Jordan washing, and Gehazi narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Naaman's military status and skin disease, the unnamed captive Israelite girl's agency, diplomatic misreading, Elisha's refusal of spectacle, Jordan washing, anti-xenophobia, Gehazi's deception and wealth-taking, and disease transfer language.

verses.restored: Naaman, commander of army of king of Aram, was a great man before his lord and lifted of face, because by him YHWH had given victory to Aram. The man was a mighty man of strength, and afflicted with a skin disease.

familiar.text: Now Naaman, captain of the host of the king of Syria, was a great man with his master, and honourable, because by him the LORD had given deliverance unto Syria: he was also a mighty man in valour, but he was a leper.

modern.text: Now Naaman, the commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a great man in his master’s sight and highly regarded, for through him the LORD had given victory to Aram. And he was a mighty man of valor, but he was a leper.

original.text: וְ֠נַעֲמָן שַׂר צְבָ֨א מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֜ם הָיָ֣ה אִישׁ֩ גָּד֨וֹל לִפְנֵ֤י אֲדֹנָיו֙ וּנְשֻׂ֣א פָנִ֔ים כִּֽי ב֛וֹ נָֽתַן יְהוָ֥ה תְּשׁוּעָ֖ה לַאֲרָ֑ם וְהָאִ֗ישׁ הָיָ֛ה גִּבּ֥וֹר חַ֖יִל מְצֹרָֽע

verses.restored: Arameans had gone out in raiding bands and captured from land of Israel a young girl, and she was before Naaman's wife.

familiar.text: And the Syrians had gone out by companies, and had brought away captive out of the land of Israel a little maid; and she waited on Naaman’s wife.

modern.text: At this time the Arameans had gone out in bands and had taken a young girl from the land of Israel, and she was serving Naaman’s wife.

original.text: וַאֲרָם֙ יָצְא֣וּ גְדוּדִ֔ים וַיִּשְׁבּ֛וּ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נַעֲרָ֣ה קְטַנָּ֑ה וַתְּהִ֕י לִפְנֵ֖י אֵ֥שֶׁת נַעֲמָֽן

verses.restored: She said to her mistress, If only my lord were before prophet who is in Samaria, then he would gather/heal him from his skin disease.

familiar.text: And she said unto her mistress, Would God my lord were with the prophet that is in Samaria! for he would recover him of his leprosy.

modern.text: She said to her mistress, “If only my master would go to the prophet who is in Samaria, he would cure him of his leprosy.”

original.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל גְּבִרְתָּ֔הּ אַחֲלֵ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י לִפְנֵ֥י הַנָּבִ֖יא אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּשֹׁמְר֑וֹן אָ֛ז יֶאֱסֹ֥ף אֹת֖וֹ מִצָּרַעְתּֽוֹ

verses.restored: He went and told his lord, saying, Thus and thus spoke the girl who is from land of Israel.

familiar.text: And one went in, and told his lord, saying, Thus and thus said the maid that is of the land of Israel.

modern.text: And Naaman went and told his master what the girl from the land of Israel had said.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֕א וַיַּגֵּ֥ד לַאדֹנָ֖יו לֵאמֹ֑ר כָּזֹ֤את וְכָזֹאת֙ דִּבְּרָ֣ה הַֽנַּעֲרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר מֵאֶ֥רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: King of Aram said, Go, enter, and I will send a letter to king of Israel. He went and took in his hand ten talents of silver, six thousand gold pieces, and ten changes of garments.

familiar.text: And the king of Syria said, Go to, go, and I will send a letter unto the king of Israel. And he departed, and took with him ten talents of silver, and six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of raiment.

modern.text: “Go now,” said the king of Aram, “and I will send you with a letter to the king of Israel.” So Naaman departed, taking with him ten talents of silver, six thousand shekels of gold, and ten sets of clothing.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָם֙ לֶךְ בֹּ֔א וְאֶשְׁלְחָ֥ה סֵ֖פֶר אֶל מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֵּלֶךְ֩ וַיִּקַּ֨ח בְּיָד֜וֹ עֶ֣שֶׂר כִּכְּרֵי כֶ֗סֶף וְשֵׁ֤שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֙ זָהָ֔ב וְעֶ֖שֶׂר חֲלִיפ֥וֹת בְּגָדִֽים

verses.restored: He brought letter to king of Israel, saying, Now when this letter comes to you, look, I have sent to you Naaman my servant so you may gather/heal him from his skin disease.

familiar.text: And he brought the letter to the king of Israel, saying, Now when this letter is come unto thee, behold, I have therewith sent Naaman my servant to thee, that thou mayest recover him of his leprosy.

modern.text: And the letter that he took to the king of Israel stated: “With this letter I am sending my servant Naaman, so that you may cure him of his leprosy.”

original.text: וַיָּבֵ֣א הַסֵּ֔פֶר אֶל מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר וְעַתָּ֗ה כְּב֨וֹא הַסֵּ֤פֶר הַזֶּה֙ אֵלֶ֔יךָ הִנֵּ֨ה שָׁלַ֤חְתִּי אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶת נַעֲמָ֣ן עַבְדִּ֔י וַאֲסַפְתּ֖וֹ מִצָּרַעְתּֽוֹ

verses.restored: It was, when king of Israel read the letter, that he tore his garments and said, Am I Divine, to put to death and make alive, that this one sends to me to gather/heal a man from his skin disease? Surely know and see that he seeks occasion against me.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when the king of Israel had read the letter, that he rent his clothes, and said, Am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man doth send unto me to recover a man of his leprosy? wherefore consider, I pray you, and see how he seeketh a quarrel against me.

modern.text: When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes and asked, “Am I God, killing and giving life, that this man expects me to cure a leper? Surely you can see that he is seeking a quarrel with me!”

original.text: וַיְהִ֡י כִּקְרֹא֩ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֨ל אֶת הַסֵּ֜פֶר וַיִּקְרַ֣ע בְּגָדָ֗יו וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הַאֱלֹהִ֥ים אָ֨נִי֙ לְהָמִ֣ית וּֽלְהַחֲי֔וֹת כִּֽי זֶה֙ שֹׁלֵ֣חַ אֵלַ֔י לֶאֱסֹ֥ף אִ֖ישׁ מִצָּֽרַעְתּ֑וֹ כִּ֤י אַךְ דְּעֽוּ נָא֙ וּרְא֔וּ כִּֽי מִתְאַנֶּ֥ה ה֖וּא לִֽי

verses.restored: It was, when Elisha man of Divine heard that king of Israel tore his garments, that he sent to king, saying, Why have you torn your garments? Let him come now to me, and he shall know there is a prophet in Israel.

familiar.text: And it was so, when Elisha the man of God had heard that the king of Israel had rent his clothes, that he sent to the king, saying, Wherefore hast thou rent thy clothes? let him come now to me, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel.

modern.text: Now when Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, he sent a message to the king: “Why have you torn your clothes? Please let the man come to me, and he will know that there is a prophet in Israel.”

original.text: וַיְהִ֞י כִּשְׁמֹ֣עַ אֱלִישָׁ֣ע אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֗ים כִּֽי קָרַ֤ע מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶת בְּגָדָ֔יו וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ לֵאמֹ֔ר לָ֥מָּה קָרַ֖עְתָּ בְּגָדֶ֑יךָ יָבֹֽא נָ֣א אֵלַ֔י וְיֵדַ֕ע כִּ֛י יֵ֥שׁ נָבִ֖יא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Naaman came with his horses and chariot and stood at entrance of house of Elisha.

familiar.text: So Naaman came with his horses and with his chariot, and stood at the door of the house of Elisha.

modern.text: So Naaman came with his horses and chariots and stood at the door of Elisha’s house.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֥א נַעֲמָ֖ן בסוסו וּבְרִכְבּ֑וֹ וַיַּעֲמֹ֥ד פֶּֽתַח הַבַּ֖יִת לֶאֱלִישָֽׁע

verses.restored: Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, Go and wash seven times in Jordan, and your flesh shall return to you, and you shall be clean.

familiar.text: And Elisha sent a messenger unto him, saying, Go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean.

modern.text: Then Elisha sent him a messenger, who said, “Go and wash yourself seven times in the Jordan, and your flesh will be restored, and you will be clean.”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח אֵלָ֛יו אֱלִישָׁ֖ע מַלְאָ֣ךְ לֵאמֹ֑ר הָל֗וֹךְ וְרָחַצְתָּ֤ שֶֽׁבַע פְּעָמִים֙ בַּיַּרְדֵּ֔ן וְיָשֹׁ֧ב בְּשָׂרְךָ֛ לְךָ֖ וּטְהָֽר

verses.restored: Naaman was angry and went away, saying, Look, I said to myself, Going out, he will surely come out to me, stand, call in name of YHWH his Divine, wave his hand over place, and gather/heal the skin disease.

familiar.text: But Naaman was wroth, and went away, and said, Behold, I thought, He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of the LORD his God, and strike his hand over the place, and recover the leper.

modern.text: But Naaman went away angry, saying, “I thought that he would surely come out, stand and call on the name of the LORD his God, and wave his hand over the spot to cure my leprosy.

original.text: וַיִּקְצֹ֥ף נַעֲמָ֖ן וַיֵּלַ֑ךְ וַיֹּאמֶר֩ הִנֵּ֨ה אָמַ֜רְתִּי אֵלַ֣י יֵצֵ֣א יָצ֗וֹא וְעָמַד֙ וְקָרָא֙ בְּשֵׁם יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔יו וְהֵנִ֥יף יָד֛וֹ אֶל הַמָּק֖וֹם וְאָסַ֥ף הַמְּצֹרָֽע

verses.restored: Are not Abanah and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all waters of Israel? Could I not wash in them and be clean? He turned and went in fury.

familiar.text: Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? may I not wash in them, and be clean? So he turned and went away in a rage.

modern.text: Are not the Abanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not have washed in them and been cleansed?” So he turned and went away in a rage.

original.text: הֲלֹ֡א טוֹב֩ אבנה וּפַרְפַּ֜ר נַהֲר֣וֹת דַּמֶּ֗שֶׂק מִכֹּל֙ מֵימֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הֲלֹֽא אֶרְחַ֥ץ בָּהֶ֖ם וְטָהָ֑רְתִּי וַיִּ֖פֶן וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ בְּחֵמָֽה

verses.restored: His servants drew near and spoke to him, saying, My father, had prophet spoken to you a great thing, would you not do it? How much more when he said to you, Wash and be clean?

familiar.text: And his servants came near, and spake unto him, and said, My father, if the prophet had bid thee do some great thing, wouldest thou not have done it? how much rather then, when he saith to thee, Wash, and be clean?

modern.text: Naaman’s servants, however, approached him and said, “My father, if the prophet had told you to do some great thing, would you not have done it? How much more, then, when he tells you, ‘Wash and be cleansed’?”

original.text: וַיִּגְּשׁ֣וּ עֲבָדָיו֮ וַיְדַבְּר֣וּ אֵלָיו֒ וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ אָבִי֙ דָּבָ֣ר גָּד֗וֹל הַנָּבִ֛יא דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יךָ הֲל֣וֹא תַעֲשֶׂ֑ה וְאַ֛ף כִּֽי אָמַ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יךָ רְחַ֥ץ וּטְהָֽר

verses.restored: He went down and dipped in Jordan seven times according to word of man of Divine, and his flesh returned like flesh of a little boy, and he was clean.

familiar.text: Then went he down, and dipped himself seven times in Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God: and his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.

modern.text: So Naaman went down and dipped himself in the Jordan seven times, according to the word of the man of God, and his flesh was restored and became like that of a little child, and he was clean. Gehazi’s Greed and Leprosy

original.text: וַיֵּ֗רֶד וַיִּטְבֹּ֤ל בַּיַּרְדֵּן֙ שֶׁ֣בַע פְּעָמִ֔ים כִּדְבַ֖ר אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַיָּ֣שָׁב בְּשָׂר֗וֹ כִּבְשַׂ֛ר נַ֥עַר קָטֹ֖ן וַיִּטְהָֽר

verses.restored: He returned to man of Divine, he and all his camp, came and stood before him, and said, Look, now I know there is no Divine in all earth except in Israel. Now please take a blessing/gift from your servant.

familiar.text: And he returned to the man of God, he and all his company, and came, and stood before him: and he said, Behold, now I know that there is no God in all the earth, but in Israel: now therefore, I pray thee, take a blessing of thy servant.

modern.text: Then Naaman and all his attendants went back to the man of God, stood before him, and declared, “Now I know for sure that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel. So please accept a gift from your servant.”

original.text: וַיָּשָׁב֩ אֶל אִ֨ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים ה֣וּא וְכָֽל מַחֲנֵ֗הוּ וַיָּבֹא֮ וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד לְפָנָיו֒ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּה נָ֤א יָדַ֨עְתִּי֙ כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין אֱלֹהִים֙ בְּכָל הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֖י אִם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְעַתָּ֛ה קַח נָ֥א בְרָכָ֖ה מֵאֵ֥ת עַבְדֶּֽךָ

verses.restored: He said, As YHWH lives, before whom I stand, I will not take. He pressed him to take, but he refused.

familiar.text: But he said, As the LORD liveth, before whom I stand, I will receive none. And he urged him to take it; but he refused.

modern.text: But Elisha replied, “As surely as the LORD lives, before whom I stand, I will not accept it.” And although Naaman urged him to accept it, he refused.

original.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר חַי יְהוָ֛ה אֲשֶׁר עָמַ֥דְתִּי לְפָנָ֖יו אִם אֶקָּ֑ח וַיִּפְצַר בּ֥וֹ לָקַ֖חַת וַיְמָאֵֽן

verses.restored: Naaman said, If not, please let there be given to your servant burden of a pair of mules of earth, for your servant will no longer make burnt offering or sacrifice to other gods, but to YHWH.

familiar.text: And Naaman said, Shall there not then, I pray thee, be given to thy servant two mules’ burden of earth? for thy servant will henceforth offer neither burnt offering nor sacrifice unto other gods, but unto the LORD.

modern.text: “If you will not,” said Naaman, “please let me, your servant, be given as much soil as a pair of mules can carry. For your servant will never again make a burnt offering or a sacrifice to any other god but the LORD.

original.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ נַעֲמָן֒ וָלֹ֕א יֻתַּן נָ֣א לְעַבְדְּךָ֔ מַשָּׂ֥א צֶֽמֶד פְּרָדִ֖ים אֲדָמָ֑ה כִּ֡י לֽוֹא יַעֲשֶׂה֩ ע֨וֹד עַבְדְּךָ֜ עֹלָ֤ה וָזֶ֨בַח֙ לֵאלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים כִּ֖י אִם לַיהוָֽה

verses.restored: For this thing may YHWH forgive your servant: when my lord enters house of Rimmon to bow there, and he leans upon my hand, and I bow in house of Rimmon—when I bow in house of Rimmon, may YHWH forgive your servant in this thing.

familiar.text: In this thing the LORD pardon thy servant, that when my master goeth into the house of Rimmon to worship there, and he leaneth on my hand, and I bow myself in the house of Rimmon: when I bow down myself in the house of Rimmon, the LORD pardon thy servant in this thing.

modern.text: Yet may the LORD forgive your servant this one thing: When my master goes into the temple of Rimmon to worship there, and he leans on my arm, and I bow down in the temple of Rimmon, may the LORD forgive your servant in this matter.”

original.text: לַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה יִסְלַ֥ח יְהוָ֖ה לְעַבְדֶּ֑ךָ בְּב֣וֹא אֲדֹנִ֣י בֵית רִמּוֹן֩ לְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֨ת שָׁ֜מָּה וְה֣וּא נִשְׁעָ֣ן עַל יָדִ֗י וְהִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֵ֨יתִי֙ בֵּ֣ית רִמֹּ֔ן בְּהִשְׁתַּחֲוָיָ֨תִי֙ בֵּ֣ית רִמֹּ֔ן יִסְלַח נא יְהוָ֥ה לְעַבְדְּךָ֖ בַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: He said to him, Go in peace. He went from him a short distance.

familiar.text: And he said unto him, Go in peace. So he departed from him a little way.

modern.text: “Go in peace,” said Elisha. But after Naaman had traveled a short distance,

verses.restored: Gehazi, servant of Elisha man of Divine, said, Look, my lord spared Naaman this Aramean by not taking from his hand what he brought. As YHWH lives, I will run after him and take something from him.

familiar.text: But Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said, Behold, my master hath spared Naaman this Syrian, in not receiving at his hands that which he brought: but, as the LORD liveth, I will run after him, and take somewhat of him.

modern.text: Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said, “Look, my master has spared this Aramean, Naaman, while not accepting what he brought. As surely as the LORD lives, I will run after him and get something from him.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר גֵּיחֲזִ֗י נַעַר֮ אֱלִישָׁ֣ע אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים֒ הִנֵּ֣ה חָשַׂ֣ךְ אֲדֹנִ֗י אֶֽת נַעֲמָ֤ן הָֽאֲרַמִּי֙ הַזֶּ֔ה מִקַּ֥חַת מִיָּד֖וֹ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר הֵבִ֑יא חַי יְהוָה֙ כִּֽי אִם רַ֣צְתִּי אַחֲרָ֔יו וְלָקַחְתִּ֥י מֵאִתּ֖וֹ מְאֽוּמָה

verses.restored: Gehazi pursued after Naaman. Naaman saw one running after him, fell from chariot to meet him, and said, Is it peace?

familiar.text: So Gehazi followed after Naaman. And when Naaman saw him running after him, he lighted down from the chariot to meet him, and said, Is all well?

modern.text: So Gehazi pursued Naaman. And when Naaman saw him running toward him, he got down from the chariot to meet him and asked, “Is everything all right?”

original.text: וַיִּרְדֹּ֥ף גֵּיחֲזִ֖י אַחֲרֵ֣י נַֽעֲמָ֑ן וַיִּרְאֶ֤ה נַֽעֲמָן֙ רָ֣ץ אַחֲרָ֔יו וַיִּפֹּ֞ל מֵעַ֧ל הַמֶּרְכָּבָ֛ה לִקְרָאת֖וֹ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הֲשָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: He said, Peace. My lord sent me, saying, Look, just now two young men from sons of prophets came to me from hill country of Ephraim. Please give them one talent of silver and two changes of garments.

familiar.text: And he said, All is well. My master hath sent me, saying, Behold, even now there be come to me from mount Ephraim two young men of the sons of the prophets: give them, I pray thee, a talent of silver, and two changes of garments.

modern.text: “Everything is all right,” Gehazi replied. “My master has sent me to say, ‘I have just now discovered that two young men from the sons of the prophets have come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Please give them a talent of silver and two sets of clothing.’”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁל֗וֹם אֲדֹנִי֮ שְׁלָחַ֣נִי לֵאמֹר֒ הִנֵּ֣ה עַתָּ֡ה זֶ֠ה בָּ֣אוּ אֵלַ֧י שְׁנֵֽי נְעָרִ֛ים מֵהַ֥ר אֶפְרַ֖יִם מִבְּנֵ֣י הַנְּבִיאִ֑ים תְּנָה נָּ֤א לָהֶם֙ כִּכַּר כֶּ֔סֶף וּשְׁתֵּ֖י חֲלִפ֥וֹת בְּגָדִֽים

verses.restored: Naaman said, Be willing, take two talents. He urged him and bound two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of garments, and gave them to two of his young men, and they carried before him.

familiar.text: And Naaman said, Be content, take two talents. And he urged him, and bound two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of garments, and laid them upon two of his servants; and they bare them before him.

modern.text: But Naaman insisted, “Please, take two talents.” And he urged Gehazi to accept them. Then he tied up two talents of silver in two bags along with two sets of clothing and gave them to two of his servants, who carried them ahead of Gehazi.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר נַעֲמָ֔ן הוֹאֵ֖ל קַ֣ח כִּכָּרָ֑יִם וַיִּפְרָץ בּ֗וֹ וַיָּצַר֩ כִּכְּרַ֨יִם כֶּ֜סֶף בִּשְׁנֵ֣י חֲרִטִ֗ים וּשְׁתֵּי֙ חֲלִפ֣וֹת בְּגָדִ֔ים וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶל שְׁנֵ֣י נְעָרָ֔יו וַיִּשְׂא֖וּ לְפָנָֽיו

verses.restored: He came to hill/Ophel, took from their hand, deposited in house, and sent men away, and they went.

familiar.text: And when he came to the tower, he took them from their hand, and bestowed them in the house: and he let the men go, and they departed.

modern.text: When Gehazi came to the hill, he took the gifts from the servants and stored them in the house. Then he dismissed the men, and they departed.

original.text: וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל הָעֹ֔פֶל וַיִּקַּ֥ח מִיָּדָ֖ם וַיִּפְקֹ֣ד בַּבָּ֑יִת וַיְשַׁלַּ֥ח אֶת הָאֲנָשִׁ֖ים וַיֵּלֵֽכוּ

verses.restored: He entered and stood before his lord. Elisha said to him, From where, Gehazi? He said, Your servant did not go here or there.

familiar.text: But he went in, and stood before his master. And Elisha said unto him, Whence comest thou, Gehazi? And he said, Thy servant went no whither.

modern.text: When Gehazi went in and stood before his master, Elisha asked him, “Gehazi, where have you been?” “Your servant did not go anywhere,” he replied.

original.text: וְהוּא בָא֙ וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד אֶל אֲדֹנָ֔יו וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ אֱלִישָׁ֔ע מאן גֵּחֲזִ֑י וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֹֽא הָלַ֥ךְ עַבְדְּךָ֖ אָ֥נֶה וָאָֽנָה

verses.restored: He said to him, Did not my heart go when man turned from upon his chariot to meet you? Is it time to take silver and garments, olive groves and vineyards, sheep and cattle, male and female servants?

familiar.text: And he said unto him, Went not mine heart with thee, when the man turned again from his chariot to meet thee? Is it a time to receive money, and to receive garments, and oliveyards, and vineyards, and sheep, and oxen, and menservants, and maidservants?

modern.text: But Elisha questioned him, “Did not my spirit go with you when the man got down from his chariot to meet you? Is this the time to accept money and clothing, olive groves and vineyards, sheep and oxen, menservants and maidservants?

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ לֹא לִבִּ֣י הָלַ֔ךְ כַּאֲשֶׁ֧ר הָֽפַךְ אִ֛ישׁ מֵעַ֥ל מֶרְכַּבְתּ֖וֹ לִקְרָאתֶ֑ךָ הַעֵ֞ת לָקַ֤חַת אֶת הַכֶּ֨סֶף֙ וְלָקַ֣חַת בְּגָדִ֔ים וְזֵיתִ֤ים וּכְרָמִים֙ וְצֹ֣אן וּבָקָ֔ר וַעֲבָדִ֖ים וּשְׁפָחֽוֹת

verses.restored: Skin disease of Naaman shall cling to you and to your seed forever. He went out from before him afflicted with skin disease, white as snow.

familiar.text: The leprosy therefore of Naaman shall cleave unto thee, and unto thy seed for ever. And he went out from his presence a leper as white as snow.

modern.text: Therefore, the leprosy of Naaman will cling to you and your descendants forever!” And as Gehazi left his presence, he was leprous—as white as snow.

original.text: וְצָרַ֤עַת נַֽעֲמָן֙ תִּֽדְבַּק בְּךָ֔ וּֽבְזַרְעֲךָ לְעוֹלָ֑ם וַיֵּצֵ֥א מִלְּפָנָ֖יו מְצֹרָ֥ע כַּשָּֽׁלֶג

translation_notes: Naaman is both an honored military commander and a person with a skin disease. Disease does not erase dignity, competence, or personhood.
The unnamed Israelite girl is a captive taken in a raid. Her insight drives the entire healing narrative, but her enslavement and displacement must not disappear behind Naaman's cure.
The Hebrew tsara'at does not equal modern leprosy/Hansen's disease by default. Use 'skin disease' pending fuller medical-historical audit and avoid contagion stigma.
YHWH giving victory to Aram complicates nationalist theology and prevents assuming Divine action belongs only to Israel's military interests.
The king misreads the letter as a diplomatic provocation, showing how illness and healing can be politicized by rulers.
Elisha refuses wealth and spectacle; healing is not sold, and prophetic authority is not validated by performance theatrics.
Naaman's servants successfully challenge his pride. Subordinates can offer wise correction without being devalued.
Naaman's request for Israelite earth reflects ancient territorial theology. His continued state duty in Rimmon's temple is met with 'Go in peace,' not coercive purity policing.
Gehazi exploits a healed foreigner through lies and invented charitable need. Religious workers may not monetize access, fabricate need, or use vulnerable people's gratitude.
The transfer of skin disease to Gehazi and his descendants is morally dangerous collective-punishment language and must not be used to explain illness, heredity, disability, or family suffering.
safety_note: Do not stigmatize skin disease, disability, foreigners, captives, servants, or interfaith complexity. Do not erase the captive girl's trauma or use Naaman's healing to glorify war. Healing is not for sale. Gehazi's punishment language may not justify disease blame, inherited guilt, or shaming families.
